speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling
text: asked the Minister for Manpower (a) since the implementation of the Progressive Wage (PW) Mark accreditation, recognising companies that pay progressive wages to lower-wage workers, how has the uptake of the PW Mark accreditation been; and (b) whether the Ministry tracks if more service buyers have chosen to do business exclusively with companies accredited with the PW Mark.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We urge all employers to pay Progressive Wages to their lower-wage workers and to apply for the PW Mark if eligible.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Manpower (Mr Zaqy Mohamad) (for the Minister for Manpower)
text: We also encourage service buyers and consumers to do their part by purchasing from PW Mark-accredited companies, where possible.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the successful roll-out of the Progressive Work Model, it is important that service buyers embrace revised wage ladders set up by the Tripartite Committee.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: It is very heartening to note that the take-up rate has been healthy for the PW Mark.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: How many employees does this translate to and the percentage of 20th percentile and below worker segments?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: I also note what Senior Minister of State had mentioned – that the Government had taken the lead and requiring for PW Mark for suppliers and sub-contractors in new Government tenders.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: In the same vein, will they also take the lead in starting the re-negotiation process for existing contracts, especially for the long-term contracts which can extend up to 10 years?

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: Additionally, there has been some feedback that some service buyers have asked for service providers to pass on or share their Progressive Wage Credit Scheme (PWCS) credits that the service providers receive during the re-negotiation process.

speaker: Ms Yeo Wan Ling (Pasir Ris-Punggol)
text: While this advisory shows that the practice is not supported and that PWCS support should instead be made transparent by service providers in the negotiation process, what pragmatic steps is the Ministry taking to safeguard service providers against such requests in the process of re-negotiations?

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, this is about 20% of the total population.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: Which I think is encouraging, given it has been implemented for the first few months.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: I think that has to be the principle.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: However, on the Government procurement, I think we are largely aligned with the Tripartite Advisory.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, the terms, conditions and the advisory given by the tripartite partners are quite clear.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: And therefore, we encourage and we certainly will make sure that our Government agencies abide by it and support this.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: On the question relating to long-term contracts and some of these unscrupulous practices, I suggest that the Tripartite Advisory is an agreement made between the Government, the Labour Movement as well as their employers.

speaker: Mr Zaqy Mohamad
text: So, if they are specific cases, I recommend the National Trades Union Congress or the Member surface them to us so that we can look into them and advise accordingly.
